title: Did I Just Set the Office On Fire?
captions: My boss said, ‘No one leaves until the report is finished,’ so I locked the door and set the fire alarm. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #office #compliance
The alarms blare. Everyone’s panicking. I’m holding my breath for the truth to surface. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #tension #whistleblower
The evacuation reveals the boss’s secret. Heroic whistleblowing or reckless sabotage? You decide. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #verdict #debate
parts: [[9:57 AM · OPEN OFFICE]] I press the red button and the alarm screams. Everyone jumps. “What the—?” someone hisses. The office lights flicker, red strobes pulse. My boss glares, “No one leaves until the report is finished.” I stare at the blinking cursor, heart pounding. [[RULE 1 · COMPLY]] I nod, smile, grab the key from my drawer. The hallway hums with coffee machines and frantic keyboards. [[3 MINUTES LEFT]] My pulse thuds; the deadline ticks down. I slip the key into the lock, turn it—click. The door slams shut behind me. [[RULE 2 · FIRE ALARM]] I race to the wall panel, slam the red button again. The shrill wail erupts louder. Red lights flood the ceiling. Sweat drips into my eyes. The PA crackles, “Evacuate immediately.” [[COUNTDOWN 2 MINUTES]] Fire doors thunder shut, sealing the floor. A colleague shoves past, breath ragged, “Did you…?” I shrug, eyes locked on the server room door, still bolted. The sprinklers sputter, a cold mist coating the carpet. A sharp ozone scent mixes with stale coffee. A muffled thump echoes from the server room. I bite my lip, waiting. The hallway lights flicker again, shadows dancing. My hand clamps the fire alarm button, fingers white. A second, then—

[[RECOVERY · HALLWAY]]
The fire alarm blares, the server room is still open, and I have only minutes before the whole building collapses.
The office erupts in shouting, flashing lights, faces twisted in panic. I stand silent, watching the exit doors swing wide. Coworkers flood out, clutching bags, phones, trembling papers.
[[RULE 3 · SILENCE]] My mouth stays shut, fingers still on the alarm. The security guard roars, “Everyone stay together!” The crowd huddles, breathing hard, eyes glued to the locked server room. The smell of melting plastic thickens.
I glance at the wall clock—seven minutes past the deadline, the alarm still screams.
[[5 MINUTES LEFT]] A junior analyst whispers, “Did you set this off on purpose?” I lock eyes with him, jaw tight. “Just following orders,” I reply, flat.
He swallows, glancing at the server door, now slightly ajar from the heat. A faint orange glow leaks out, illuminating rows of humming drives.
The guard’s radio crackles, “Breach in server room. Possible data loss.” Tension spikes. Sprinklers hiss louder, water pooling at my shoes. A cold draft seeps from the doorway, as if something unseen is breathing.
Suddenly, metal tears—shelf collapses with a deafening crash. The alarm’s shriek climbs.
My pulse pounds. A distant siren wails, growing nearer. The building shudders.
I hold my breath, waiting for the next move.
[[END PART 2]]

[[EVACUATION · LOBBY]] The building’s lobby erupts into a frenzy of police, fire trucks, and flashing lights. My coworkers cluster, eyes glued to the server room’s cracked door. The guard yells, “Secure the area!” I step forward, the fire alarm still blaring in my ears. [[RULE 4 · REVEAL]] The door bursts open, and a fireman pulls out a metal box, spilling papers onto the floor. Among them, a ledger—numbers, signatures, and a red stamp: “EMBEZZLED.” The boss’s name is at the top, underlined in ink. The crowd gasps. My heart pounds. The fire alarm finally stops, a low hum fading. I watch as the fire brigade seals the server room, sealing away the evidence. The police handcuff my boss, his face pale, eyes darting at the ledger. I feel a wave of relief, then a flicker of doubt. A coworker grips my arm, “You could’ve killed us.” I swallow, “I followed his exact words.” The sirens wail louder, the night air cold against my skin. The building’s lights dim, the emergency exit signs blinking. I stand alone, the weight of what I did settling like dust. The debate burns inside me—heroic whistleblowing or reckless sabotage? I glance at the ledger one last time, the truth laid bare. The camera zooms on my face, eyes searching. “So… was I wrong?” [[END PART 3]]

premise.hook: My boss said, ‘No one leaves until the report is finished,’ so I locked the office door and set the fire alarm.
premise.twist: The fire alarm triggers a building-wide evacuation, exposing the boss’s embezzlement hidden in the locked server room.
premise.debate: Was the narrator’s extreme compliance heroic whistleblowing or dangerous sabotage that endangered coworkers?
